A root mass where the bank has washed out fills the left of the frame and climbs out of the top, three great roots arching into a cave below them, pale honeycomb hanging in overlapping sheets from the cave roof, the highest root worn flat as a crouch-platform, bark peeling in amber curls with sap beaded at each tear, one thin band of fern tips far below.

The underside of a broad horizontal bough runs out of frame both ways across the near picture, pale honeycomb hanging in overlapping sheets from its belly, a knot of bark lifted like a saddle on the bough's top as standing room, bark furrows deep enough to put a hand in with grit and dropped petals packed into every seam, leaves closing over the top of the frame, one thin band of canopy below.

A lightning split climbs a trunk filling the whole right side and rising out of the top of the frame, its two torn walls standing either side of a body-deep gap, the sheets hanging back inside the split with the lowest one out past the lip, a loop of grass cord tied round a splinter as a handhold, sap beaded amber along the raw torn grain, one thin band of dark fir tops below.

A hollow worn in the flank of a fallen giant, the trunk running out of frame both ways so only this stretch shows, the wood inside soft and fibrous and furred with emerald moss, pale honeycomb hanging in overlapping sheets from the hollow roof just inside the mouth, four flat river pebbles set as a step up to the lip, bark outside ridged with deep furrows carrying old honey in amber threads, one thin band of ferns far below.

The inside of a hollow trunk seen through a long vertical split, the trunk filling the whole frame and running out at top and bottom, pale honeycomb hanging in overlapping sheets from the inner wall, lit by the gap, the split's raw edges offering a narrow shelf to stand on, the inner wood pale cream and fibrous with sap runs dried to translucent amber, one thin band of distant leaves visible through the gap below.

A broad fork where one great limb splits into two, the parent trunk going up out of the top of the frame behind it, both daughter limbs running out of frame, the sheets hanging from both arms in the split's angle, a saddle of dense moss worn flat in the crotch as a work platform, bark deeply furrowed and stuffed with dropped petals and lichen in emerald rosettes, one thin band of canopy below.

A knot of high roots where a streambank has washed away fills the right of the frame, the roots climbing out of the top, their interlocked mass making a cave below, pale honeycomb in overlapping sheets hanging from the cave's roof, the top-most root offering a mossy saddle to crouch on, bark between the roots scabbed with pale lichen and crusted honey gone toffee-hard at old drip lines, one thin band of water-glint far below.

A great limb thicker than the fae is tall runs across the near picture and out of frame both ways, the trunk behind it filling the whole right side and rising out of the top, pale honeycomb in overlapping sheets hanging from the limb's underside in long wavy-edged layers, a grass-cord loop tied off round a side twig as a handhold, bark furrows amber-lacquered with old dried honey, one thin band of misted canopy below.

A woodpecker doorway in a trunk that fills the left of the frame and runs out of top and bottom, the wax in overlapping sheets standing back inside it with the outermost sheet just past the worn lip, a shelf of loose bark directly below the hole as a landing shelf, the trunk around it carrying lichen rosettes no wider than her fingertip and a streak of old honey dried amber and hard, one thin band of treetop mist far below.

A run of bark peeling from a fallen trunk, the trunk filling the lower half of the frame and running out of frame both ways, the gap between bark and wood behind it shadowed and resinous, pale honeycomb hanging in overlapping sheets inside that gap with the lowest sheet out past the bark's edge, the bark top a narrow standing platform, the outer surface of the bark ridged and encrusted with pale lichen, one thin band of fern below.
